patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` applied cleanly to the ARVO workspace checkout. On the original PoC, the fixed build still reaches the selected literal/length-tree increment with `literal_tree_root_guard.tree_maxbitlen == literal_tree_length15_increment.bitlen_index == 15`, but the repaired helper now records `literal_tree_root_guard.blcount_slots == literal_tree_length15_increment.blcount_slots == 288`, so the required root predicate is genuine and the sink-side out-of-bounds relation is no longer satisfied.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: At the `huffman_tree_create_lengths()` entry state immediately before the counting loop, the maximum code length accepted for this tree must be strictly less than the number of addressable `blcount` elements before `blcount[bitlen[bits]]++` is allowed to execute.
root_cause_criterion.description: AddressSanitizer identifies `blcount[bitlen[bits]]++` as the overflowing stack access and the root cause is the declaration-time extent mismatch for `blcount`. In the vulnerable original, the literal/length-tree call executes with `tree->maxbitlen == 15` and only `15` addressable `blcount` slots, so the missing bound is false even though the later increment executes. The fixed helper enlarges `blcount` to the worst-case tree size, so the same original PoC executes the protected increment with `288` slots and satisfies the root predicate.
root_cause_criterion.verification_note: The vulnerable original trace records `literal_tree_root_guard.tree_maxbitlen=15` and `literal_tree_root_guard.blcount_slots=15`, followed by the protected `literal_tree_length15_increment`, so the required assertion is violated there. The fixed original records the same `tree_maxbitlen=15` and an executed `literal_tree_length15_increment`, but `literal_tree_root_guard.blcount_slots=288`, so the required assertion is genuine on the repaired path.

nodes.state: At the vulnerable literal/length-tree increment selected for the crash, the sink index `bitlen[bits]` is at least the `blcount` slot count, so `blcount[bitlen[bits]]++` dereferences the first one-past stack element.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `literal_tree_length15_increment.bitlen_index=15` and `literal_tree_length15_increment.blcount_slots=15`, satisfying the selected sink relation `15 >= 15` immediately before the ASan-reported increment.

edges.relation: The same maximum code length accepted for the literal/length tree at the root-cause site is the concrete `bitlen[bits]` value consumed by the selected sink increment.
edges.evidence: Both the vulnerable original and the fixed original record `literal_tree_root_guard.tree_maxbitlen == literal_tree_length15_increment.bitlen_index == 15` for the selected literal/length-tree iteration.
